agate.name: Agate
aliases: agatized wood (a loose trade term, see S2)
agate.colors: Brown, white, red, gray, pink, black and yellow, often in alternating bands.

alexandrite.name: Alexandrite
alexandrite.colors: Green to bluish green in daylight, red to purplish red in incandescent light (fine material).
alexandrite.birthstone: June birthstone, with pearl and moonstone.

amazonite.name: Amazonite
amazonite.colors: Pale to dark green and blue-green, often with white mottling or streaks.

amber.name: Amber
amber.colors: Typically yellow, orange and brown. Rare pieces can be green, blue or violet-tinted.

amethyst.name: Amethyst
amethyst.colors: Purple by definition, from barely perceptible lilac to deep reddish purple. Reddish purple with rich saturation is the most popular.

ammonite.name: Ammonite
ammonite.colors: Black, brown and multi-color per S2.

apatite.name: Apatite
apatite.colors: Green, brown, blue, yellow, violet, pink, colorless. Neon blue-green from Madagascar is the prized color.

apophyllite.name: Apophyllite
apophyllite.colors: Usually white or colorless; also blue, green, brown, yellow, pink, violet.

aqua-aura-quartz.name: Aqua Aura Quartz
aqua-aura-quartz.colors: Electric blue and teal to violet and gold, shifting with viewing angle and light. Thicker films go deeper blue or violet.

aquamarine.name: Aquamarine
aquamarine.colors: Greenish blue to blue, from very faint to rich and vibrant. Rich blue is the most popular, rarest and most valuable.
aquamarine.birthstone: March birthstone; geology.com adds that bloodstone is the other March choice.

aragonite.name: Aragonite
aragonite.colors: Many colors, commonly red or white; faceted gems are usually colorless or straw-yellow; blue material comes from Greece and Chile.

atlantisite.name: Atlantisite
atlantisite.colors: Dominant colors are green from serpentine and purple from stichtite, with black from chromite and magnetite.
atlantisite.chakra: Stichtite and Atlantisite are called crown chakra stones (S2).
atlantisite.birthstone: Stichtite is not a traditional birthstone.

aura-quartz.name: Aura Quartz
aura-quartz.colors: Gold, silver, rainbow and opal per S4; rainbow of colors with blues, purples and greens usually dominant per S5.
aura-quartz.chakra: All chakras per S4; all seven per S5.
aura-quartz.birthstone: April birthstone, or a stand-in for amethyst as February birthstone, per S5 (mystic quartz).

azurite.name: Azurite
azurite.colors: Deep blue to violet-blue, the shade called azure.

bicolor-tourmaline.name: Bicolor Tourmaline
bicolor-tourmaline.colors: Tourmaline occurs in every color; bicolor stones pair two, such as pink and yellow, or red crystals with green tips.
bicolor-tourmaline.birthstone: Tourmaline in general is the birthstone for October.

black-agate.name: Black Agate
black-agate.colors: Agate in general includes black among brown, white, red, gray, pink and yellow. Pure black chalcedony is rare and most black material is dyed.

black-jade.name: Black Jade
black-jade.colors: Very dark forest green to essentially opaque black, depending on iron and thickness.

black-moonstone.name: Black Moonstone
black-moonstone.colors: Moonstone in general: white, gray, brown, pink, orange, green, yellow, colorless; no source lists black.
black-moonstone.birthstone: Moonstone in general is a June birthstone, one of the original modern birthstones of 1912.

black-tourmaline.name: Black Tourmaline
black-tourmaline.colors: Black, bluish-black, brownish-black or greenish-black; black is the most common tourmaline color.

bloodstone.name: Bloodstone
bloodstone.colors: Dark green base with red to orange spots; other spot colors (white, yellow, brown) occur.
bloodstone.birthstone: Traditional March birthstone; modern birthstone for March since 1912 per S2.

blue-apatite.name: Blue Apatite
blue-apatite.colors: Apatite in general comes in green, brown, blue, yellow, violet, pink and colorless. Blue gems also include neon blue-green material.

blue-aragonite.name: Blue Aragonite
blue-aragonite.colors: Aragonite in general: vibrant blue and green aragonite are prized for vivid hues; commonly red or white.
blue-aragonite.chakra: Aragonite in general: associated with the root and sacral chakras.

blue-aventurine.name: Blue Aventurine
blue-aventurine.colors: Aventurine is most often green; blue is named as one of the other, less common colors.
blue-aventurine.chakra: S4 links aventurine to the brow and crown chakras; S1 links green aventurine to the heart chakra. Nothing on blue specifically.

blue-calcite.name: Blue Calcite
blue-calcite.colors: Calcite in general is usually white but can also be colorless, gray, red, green, blue, yellow, brown or orange.

blue-chalcedony.name: Blue Chalcedony
blue-chalcedony.colors: Blue chalcedony runs pale to medium blue, modified by gray or pink. Unstained chalcedony is often grayish blue. Pure deep blue is the most valuable color per S3.
blue-chalcedony.chakra: Throat Chakra per S3 (a modern belief).

blue-jade.name: Blue Jade
blue-jade.colors: Jade comes in many colors including blue. S3 lists blue among jadeite colors.

blue-lace-agate.name: Blue Lace Agate
blue-lace-agate.chakra: A dealer site pairs it with amethyst for the throat chakra.

blue-onyx.name: Blue Onyx
blue-onyx.colors: Onyx in general: black mostly, also brown, red, white, grayish blue and green; niccolo onyx has light blue or gray bands on black.
blue-onyx.chakra: Black onyx is linked to the root chakra per S2; nothing on blue onyx.
blue-onyx.birthstone: Onyx in general: modern February birthstone per S2 (not specific to blue onyx).

blue-opal.name: Blue Opal
blue-opal.colors: Pale sky blue, seafoam to deeper teal. Peruvian opal comes in pastel blues, greens and pinks.
blue-opal.birthstone: Opal in general is the October birthstone. The sources do not say this for blue opal specifically.

blue-tigers-eye.name: Blue Tiger's Eye
blue-tigers-eye.colors: Natural hawk's eye is grayish-blue. Some pieces mix blue and golden brown.

bornite.name: Bornite
bornite.colors: Reddish brown or brownish red when fresh; iridescent purple, blue and black when tarnished.

botryoidal-hematite.name: Botryoidal Hematite
botryoidal-hematite.colors: Hematite in general: black to steel-gray to silver, or red to reddish brown; the streak is red to reddish brown.

botswana-agate.name: Botswana Agate
botswana-agate.colors: Gray, white or brown body with stripes of soft blues, pinks and greens. Orange, pink and green versions exist.
botswana-agate.chakra: Root chakra per S4. Pink Botswana agate is tied to the heart chakra.

brecciated-jasper.name: Brecciated Jasper
brecciated-jasper.colors: Jasper in general can come in any color.

brown-jasper.name: Brown Jasper
brown-jasper.colors: Jasper in general is colored by various mineral impurities, and many jaspers are named after their color. The sources never describe brown jasper.

bumblebee-jasper.name: Bumblebee Jasper
bumblebee-jasper.colors: Bright yellow to orange bands with black, often as bull's-eye (orbicular) patterns.

calcite.name: Calcite
calcite.colors: Usually white, but also colorless, gray, red, green, blue, yellow, brown or orange.

carnelian.name: Carnelian
carnelian.colors: Yellow-orange to rich reddish orange to orangey brown. Often banded red-orange with white agate bands.

cats-eye.name: Cat's Eye
cats-eye.colors: Chatoyant chrysoberyl can be honey to light yellow, greenish or dark yellowish-brown; S1 describes a brownish green example.

celestite.name: Celestite
celestite.colors: Mainly sky blue. Also colorless, white, pink, pale green, yellow, orange, brown and red. Gems are usually colorless or pale blue.
celestite.chakra: A dealer says it opens the throat, third eye and crown chakras.

charoite.name: Charoite
charoite.colors: Purple to violet, light brown, weathering to chalky white; swirls of orange, greenish gray, greenish black and white from other minerals.

chevron-amethyst.name: Chevron Amethyst
chevron-amethyst.colors: Amethyst in general ranges from light to deep purple. Banding and zoning of the color are common in amethyst crystals.
chevron-amethyst.birthstone: Amethyst in general is the February birthstone.

chiastolite.name: Chiastolite
chiastolite.colors: Black cross or featherlike graphite pattern with four radiating arms.

chlorite.name: Chlorite
chlorite.colors: Various shades of green; rarely yellow, white, pink or black.

chrysoberyl.name: Chrysoberyl
chrysoberyl.colors: Usually brown, pale yellow, yellow-green and green; bright yellow and yellow-green are the most desirable shades per S1.
chrysoberyl.birthstone: Alexandrite, the color-change variety, is a June birthstone (added in 1952). Plain chrysoberyl is not named.

chrysocolla.name: Chrysocolla
chrysocolla.colors: Blue, cyan (blue-green), green, dark blue to black, brown, rarely yellow.
chrysocolla.birthstone: Not a traditional birthstone; suggested as an alternative to turquoise, December's birthstone.

chrysoprase.name: Chrysoprase
chrysoprase.colors: Apple to olive green and nearly pure medium greens; pale yellowish green to deeply saturated green.
chrysoprase.birthstone: Kunz says the foundation-stone scheme gives chrysoprase for December, but the month list gives ruby instead.

citrine.name: Citrine
citrine.colors: Yellow to orangey yellow, yellowish orange and brownish orange. Reddish orange and reddish brown are rare and often called Madeira.
citrine.chakra: Used as the solar plexus chakra stone per S3.
citrine.birthstone: November, along with topaz. S3 says citrine was added to the modern list in 1952.

clear-quartz.name: Clear Quartz
clear-quartz.colors: Colorless. Quartz in general occurs in almost every color.
clear-quartz.chakra: A dealer says it cleanses all seven chakras.

coral.name: Coral
coral.colors: Calcareous coral comes in white, red and pink; conchiolin coral in black, brown and gold; blue coral is rare.

crazy-lace-agate.name: Crazy Lace Agate
crazy-lace-agate.colors: Crazy Lace shows very fine banding with contrasting colors. Agate in general comes in brown, white, red, gray, pink, black and yellow.

dalmatian-jasper.name: Dalmatian Jasper
dalmatian-jasper.colors: White to cream base with black spots; S4 adds brown spots. Spots rarely exceed 4 mm.

danburite.name: Danburite
danburite.colors: Colorless to light yellow, pale pink or tan; rare dark blue cat's eye.
danburite.chakra: Said to help open the heart, third eye and crown chakras (S3, dealer source).

diamond.name: Diamond
diamond.colors: Most diamonds are brown or yellow; colorless is favored by jewelers; vivid colors are extremely rare.

dolomite.name: Dolomite
aliases: dolostone (the rock, distinct from the mineral)
dolomite.colors: Colorless, white, pink, green, gray, brown, black.

dragon-blood-jasper.name: Dragon Blood Jasper
dragon-blood-jasper.colors: Deep forest-green with bold streaks and splashes of blood-red.

druzy.name: Druzy
druzy.colors: Usually white, red, orange, yellow or brown; sometimes purple, green, blue, pink or black. Dyes can give any color.
druzy.chakra: Crystal healers link druzy quartz to the crown chakra (S1).
druzy.birthstone: Depends on the quartz color, e.g. citrine for November, amethyst for February (S1).

elestial-quartz.name: Elestial Quartz
elestial-quartz.colors: Colorless, brown or gray with multi-colored clay inclusions; natural golden (citrine) or purple (amethyst) colors are much rarer.

emerald.name: Emerald
emerald.colors: Distinctly green, from bluish green to slightly yellowish green; lighter or weaker stones are called green beryl.

epidote.name: Epidote
epidote.colors: Usually yellowish green to pistachio green; less often brownish green to black.

fancy-jasper.name: Fancy Jasper
fancy-jasper.colors: Jasper in general can come in any color.

fire-agate.name: Fire Agate
fire-agate.colors: Brown with red, orange, yellow and green iridescent flashes.

flower-agate.name: Flower Agate
flower-agate.colors: Mostly pink, peach or white, sometimes gray, brown, red, green or orange. Often pinks, creams and whites.
flower-agate.chakra: Root and heart chakras in modern belief (S6).

fluorite.name: Fluorite
fluorite.colors: Typically purple, green, yellow; also colorless, blue, red, black. Pink and chrome green are rare.

galena.name: Galena
galena.colors: Bright silver on fresh surfaces, tarnishing to dull lead gray.

garnet.name: Garnet
garnet.colors: Typically red, but also orange, green, yellow, purple, black or brown; blue garnets are extremely rare.
garnet.birthstone: January birthstone. Kunz notes that old lists had the garnet for January instead of the jacinth.

gold-tigers-eye.name: Gold Tiger's Eye
gold-tigers-eye.colors: Golden to red-brown in general; S3 lists reddish brown, golden brown, blue and grey.

golden-healer-quartz.name: Golden Healer Quartz
golden-healer-quartz.colors: Quartz in general occurs in virtually every color, including yellow. No source gives the color of golden healer quartz.

golden-lepidolite.name: Golden Lepidolite
golden-lepidolite.colors: Lepidolite in general runs from pale pink to deep purple with a greyish tint; no gold color is mentioned.
golden-lepidolite.chakra: Lepidolite in general is thought to balance the throat chakra (S1).

golden-sheen-obsidian.name: Golden Sheen Obsidian
golden-sheen-obsidian.colors: Golden or silvery sheen over dark (black or brown) glass.

grape-agate.name: Grape Agate
grape-agate.colors: Mostly dull gray, brown or colorless; only about 10% has attractive color, mainly purple, then green or blue-green.

gray-agate.name: Gray Agate
gray-agate.colors: Agate in general includes brown, white, red, gray, pink, black and yellow, in alternating bands.

green-aventurine.name: Green Aventurine
green-aventurine.colors: Mostly green; also orange, yellow, red, pink, brown, white, gray and blue. Often banded light and dark.
green-aventurine.chakra: Green aventurine is often used for the heart chakra (S1). S3 gives brow and crown chakras for aventurine in general.

green-calcite.name: Green Calcite
green-calcite.colors: Calcite in general is usually white or colorless, with green among its light shades. S5 describes green calcite from pale mint to deeper green.

green-jade.name: Green Jade
green-jade.colors: Jade in general occurs in many colors; jadeite ranges from white to dark green and nephrite from white and cream to dark green.

green-opal.name: Green Opal
green-opal.colors: Prase opal is apple-green; prase opals in general run green to yellowish green. Opal in general: white, gray and green are the most common body colors.
green-opal.birthstone: Opal in general is an October birthstone.

green-quartz.name: Green Quartz
green-quartz.colors: Leek green, yellow-green or golden green. Natural stones are often very light. Darker green is generally treated.

hematite.name: Hematite
hematite.colors: Black or gray most commonly; also steel gray, silver, red and reddish brown. Always a reddish streak.

hemimorphite.name: Hemimorphite
hemimorphite.colors: Usually white, brown, gray or colorless. Sometimes spectacular blue, greenish blue or green.

howlite.name: Howlite
howlite.colors: White to light gray, with gray, black or dark brown web-like veins; crystals can be colorless or, rarely, brown. Often dyed other colors, most commonly robin's egg blue.

imperial-topaz.name: Imperial Topaz
imperial-topaz.colors: Reddish orange to orangy red (S2), medium reddish orange to orange-red (S4), highly saturated reddish orange (S1). S3 says yellow, pink or pink-orange.
imperial-topaz.birthstone: Topaz is the November birthstone (S2). S3 says orange topaz, also called precious topaz, holds that role.

indicolite.name: Indicolite
indicolite.colors: Shades of blue, sometimes with green undertones; blue to bluish green.
indicolite.birthstone: October birthstone (as a tourmaline), per S2.

indigo-gabbro.name: Indigo Gabbro
indigo-gabbro.colors: Mottled black, gray and white. The source does not mention an indigo color.
indigo-gabbro.chakra: Third Eye and Root (traditional, per the dealer).

iolite.name: Iolite
iolite.colors: Blue, violet-blue, blue-violet, yellowish gray, colorless and brown. Strongly pleochroic: violet, colorless to yellow, light grayish blue.

jade.name: Jade
jade.colors: Most known as green, but also white, lavender, yellow, blue, black, red, orange and gray. Nephrite is usually white, cream to dark green.

jasper.name: Jasper
jasper.colors: Most commonly red, yellow, brown, green; very rarely blue. Names come from color, pattern or place.

kambaba-jasper.name: Kambaba Jasper
kambaba-jasper.colors: Green, with blackish, irregularly shaped orbs.

kunzite.name: Kunzite
kunzite.colors: Pastel pink to intense violetish purple.
kunzite.birthstone: Some consider kunzite an alternate birthstone for February.

kyanite.name: Kyanite
kyanite.colors: Mostly blue. Also white, gray, green, colorless, and sometimes pink, yellow, orange or black. May show color zones.

labradorite.name: Labradorite
labradorite.colors: Body color usually clear, white or gray; labradorescent flashes of blue, green, yellow, orange and red.

lapis-lazuli.name: Lapis Lazuli
lapis-lazuli.colors: Greenish blue to violetish blue; from grayish blue to royal blue to deep indigo, with white calcite and gold pyrite.

larimar.name: Larimar
larimar.colors: White, sky blue, deep blue and blue-green, often with white splotches; green, brown or red tones also occur.
larimar.birthstone: Can substitute for turquoise as a December birthstone.

larvikite.name: Larvikite
larvikite.colors: Black, blue, brown, gray and white per S2, with a silver-blue sheen on polished surfaces.

lava-rock.name: Lava Rock
lava-rock.colors: Black or dark gray to deep reddish brown; also brown or purplish red.

lavender-jade.name: Lavender Jade
lavender-jade.colors: Jadeite occurs in many colors including lavender, lilac, pink, green and white.

lemon-quartz.name: Lemon Quartz
lemon-quartz.colors: Citrine runs from pale lemon to deep golden honey per S4, and from light yellow to dark yellow and gold-brown per S5.

lemurian-quartz.name: Lemurian Quartz
lemurian-quartz.colors: Usually sold as clear quartz crystals.

leopardskin-jasper.name: Leopardskin Jasper
leopardskin-jasper.colors: Light brown to deep red per S3; S4 describes black-outlined spots on a yellow-brown base with brown centers.

lepidolite.name: Lepidolite
lepidolite.colors: Usually pink, red or purple, often grayish. Rarely colorless or yellow.

magnesite.name: Magnesite
magnesite.colors: White, grayish, yellowish, brownish, rarely colorless.

mahogany-obsidian.name: Mahogany Obsidian
mahogany-obsidian.colors: Deep brown to black with reddish-brown patches, streaks or swirls. The common mix is black and brown swirled together.
mahogany-obsidian.chakra: Modern belief links it to the lower three chakras (S4).

malachite.name: Malachite
malachite.colors: Always green, from pastel through bright to very dark green that is almost black, often banded.

mangano-calcite.name: Mangano Calcite
mangano-calcite.colors: Pale pink, rose pink or peach.

marcasite.name: Marcasite
marcasite.colors: Pale bronze yellow to silvery yellow when fresh, tarnishing brownish.

meteorite.name: Meteorite
meteorite.colors: The thin fusion crust is black on most meteorites; very light on some achondrites.

mexican-fire-opal.name: Mexican Fire Opal
mexican-fire-opal.colors: Orange, yellow, red, brown or a combination; Mexico is best known for bright yellow, orange and red fire opal.
mexican-fire-opal.chakra: Yellow fire opal is tied to the solar plexus chakra (S5).
mexican-fire-opal.birthstone: Fire opal is described as an April birthstone and an alternative to opal for October (S5); opal in general is an October birthstone (S1).

moldavite.name: Moldavite
moldavite.colors: Green, from olive and yellowish green to bottle green; S2 adds greenish brown.

mookaite-jasper.name: Mookaite Jasper
mookaite-jasper.colors: Brown, multi-color, pink, purple, red and yellow.

moonstone.name: Moonstone
moonstone.colors: Body colors include white, gray, brown, pink, orange, green, yellow and colorless. The sheen is usually white to silvery, rarely blue.
moonstone.birthstone: A June birthstone with pearl and alexandrite, among the original modern birthstones of 1912. Preferred over them in Germany and Scandinavia.

morganite.name: Morganite
morganite.colors: Pink, purplish pink or orangy pink, often light in tone. S3 gives a range from slightly yellowish orange to slightly purplish pink.

moss-agate.name: Moss Agate
moss-agate.colors: Clear or milky white with green moss-like inclusions; S5 adds cream, green-grey and black patterns, and red from iron in Montana stones.
moss-agate.chakra: Usually connected with the Heart Chakra per S5.

nuummite.name: Nuummite
nuummite.colors: Black, gray or brownish-black, with blue, red, green, violet or golden-yellow iridescent flecks.

obsidian.name: Obsidian
obsidian.colors: Black is most common. Also brown, tan and green. Rarely blue, red, orange or yellow.

ocean-jasper.name: Ocean Jasper
ocean-jasper.colors: Green, brown, yellow, cream, red or pink backgrounds with colorful orbs; orbs usually show concentric bands of slightly or distinctly different color.

onyx.name: Onyx
onyx.colors: Black (mainly), brown, red, white, grayish blue, green; classic form is black and white bands.
onyx.birthstone: February (traditional per S4, modern per S5); sardonyx was an old August stone.

opal.name: Opal
opal.colors: Body color can be any color, commonly white, yellow, gray, black or brown. Precious opal adds a spectral play of color.

orange-calcite.name: Orange Calcite
orange-calcite.colors: Calcite in general is usually white, but can be colorless, gray, red, green, blue, yellow, brown or orange.

orca-agate.name: Orca Agate
orca-agate.colors: Agate in general shows every color, including red, blue, orange, black, white, gray, yellow, pink, brown and multi-color. No source gives the colors of orca agate.

peach-moonstone.name: Peach Moonstone
peach-moonstone.colors: Peach ranges from light apricot to rich peach with a silvery or pearly sheen (S5). Moonstone overall spans white, gray, brown, pink, orange, green, yellow and colorless (S3).
peach-moonstone.birthstone: Moonstone in general is a June birthstone with pearl and alexandrite.

pearl.name: Pearl
pearl.colors: White and cream most familiar; also black, gray, yellow, orange, pink, lavender, green, blue.
pearl.birthstone: June birthstone, and gem of the third and thirtieth anniversaries per GIA.

peridot.name: Peridot
peridot.colors: Mostly yellowish green; the best is pure grass green. Iron-rich fayalite is brown.
peridot.birthstone: August birthstone per GIA. Kunz (1913) says chrysolite (peridot) was long the gem of September, and calls its move to August an alternate.

petrified-wood.name: Petrified Wood
petrified-wood.colors: White, yellowish, banded, brownish, black (charred), also bright colors; chromium gives green.

phantom-quartz.name: Phantom Quartz
phantom-quartz.colors: Phantom zones can show different colors, including blood red from hematite.

pietersite.name: Pietersite
pietersite.colors: Almost always multi-colored, mostly blue or brown with golden yellow, white or black. Chinese stones are mostly reddish-brown per S1.
pietersite.chakra: S2 says it aligns all the chakras.
pietersite.birthstone: An alternative August birthstone per S2.

pink-opal.name: Pink Opal
pink-opal.colors: Pale pink, pink and dark red-pink per S7. Peruvian material is pastel pink, often with blue and green stones.
pink-opal.birthstone: Opal in general is an October birthstone. Pink opal is not named separately.

pink-tourmaline.name: Pink Tourmaline
pink-tourmaline.colors: Pale pink, rose, salmon, raspberry, magenta and reddish-pink.
pink-tourmaline.birthstone: Tourmaline in general is a birthstone for October (parent-level).

prasiolite.name: Prasiolite
prasiolite.colors: Yellow-green to green; much of the material sold is light in color, with rich green mostly in stones of a few carats.

prehnite-epidote.name: Prehnite with Epidote
prehnite-epidote.colors: Epidote runs yellowish green to brownish black; prehnite is light green, oil-green, gray, white or colorless. Wisconsin prehnite fillings range white to green to pale pink.

prehnite.name: Prehnite
prehnite.colors: Light green to yellow, also colorless, blue, pink or white; rare orange found in 2000.
prehnite.chakra: A dealer site says prehnite balances the heart chakra and solar plexus chakra.

purple-jade.name: Purple Jade
purple-jade.colors: The GIA bead was mottled purple with fibrous lavender grains and a brownish white component. Jade in general also occurs in lavender.

pyrite.name: Pyrite
pyrite.colors: Brass yellow, often tarnished to dull brass. Streak greenish black to brownish black.

rainbow-fluorite.name: Rainbow Fluorite
rainbow-fluorite.colors: Rainbow fluorite shows several colors in one stone. Fluorite in general is typically purple, green and yellow, also colorless, blue, red and black.
rainbow-fluorite.chakra: Fluorite in general is traditionally linked to the third eye, heart and throat chakras per dealer S5.

rainbow-lattice-sunstone.name: Rainbow Lattice Sunstone
rainbow-lattice-sunstone.colors: Pale yellow to colorless, with pink, green and orange variations, plus golden and rainbow flashes.

rainbow-moonstone.name: Rainbow Moonstone
rainbow-moonstone.colors: Blue sheen (royal blue in the trade) or multicolored sheen (rainbow).
rainbow-moonstone.birthstone: Orthoclase (true) moonstone is an alternate June birthstone with pearl; the source does not say this for labradorite.

rainforest-jasper.name: Rainforest Jasper
rainforest-jasper.colors: Shades of green, brown, red and cream (S3); green, red, yellow, brown and orange (S4).

red-aventurine.name: Red Aventurine
red-aventurine.colors: Aventurine in general is most often green but also red, orange, pink, brown and more. Hematite inclusions are typically red-brown or gold-brown.
red-aventurine.chakra: Aventurine in general: brow and crown per S3; green aventurine represents the heart chakra per S1. Red aventurine is not addressed.

red-beryl.name: Red Beryl
red-beryl.colors: Pink to deeply saturated red; best faceted stones are raspberry pink to slightly purplish red.

red-jade.name: Red Jade
red-jade.colors: S1 and S3 list red among jadeite colors. S4's color list (green, white, orange, yellow, lavender, grey, black) omits red.

red-jasper.name: Red Jasper
red-jasper.colors: Red from iron oxide. Jasper in general can come in any color.

rhodochrosite.name: Rhodochrosite
rhodochrosite.colors: Pink, red, yellow, gray and brown. Aggregates can show white or grey bands.

rhodolite.name: Rhodolite Garnet
rhodolite.colors: Mostly purplish red; can range from purplish red to reddish, almost pure purple. Purple stones like amethyst found in North Carolina and India.
rhodolite.chakra: Root, heart and crown chakras per S2.
rhodolite.birthstone: January birthstone, as for all garnets.

rhodonite.name: Rhodonite
rhodonite.colors: Pink, red, and reddish brown to brown when weathered.

rose-quartz.name: Rose Quartz
aliases: pink quartz (a rarer, different type per S2 and S3)
rose-quartz.colors: Very light pink, almost white, to medium-dark pink. Larger pieces show the deepest color.

ruby-fuchsite.name: Ruby Fuchsite
ruby-fuchsite.colors: Green fuchsite with red, sometimes pink or purplish, ruby areas.
ruby-fuchsite.birthstone: Ruby is associated with July, so the material may appeal as a July birthstone option.

ruby-zoisite.name: Ruby Zoisite
ruby-zoisite.colors: Green chrome-zoisite, black amphibole and reddish ruby.
ruby-zoisite.chakra: Third eye and heart chakras per one seller passage, heart and crown per its FAQ. The sources disagree.

ruby.name: Ruby
ruby.colors: Orangy red through strongly purplish red; fine gems are a pure, vibrant red to slightly purplish red.

sapphire.name: Sapphire
sapphire.colors: Blue is best known. Fancy sapphires come in violet, green, yellow, orange, pink, purple, and can be gray, black or brown.

sardonyx.name: Sardonyx
sardonyx.colors: Usually yellow-brown or red-brown bands with white. S3 lists white to orange and red to black.
sardonyx.chakra: S3 links white and red-brown sardonyx to the crown chakra.
sardonyx.birthstone: Traditional August birthstone per S2. S3 names it one of three August stones. Kunz 1913 calls it an alternate for August.

scolecite.name: Scolecite
scolecite.colors: Usually colorless or white; can be pink, salmon, red or green.
scolecite.chakra: Said to open the third eye chakra (S2, dealer source).

selenite.name: Selenite
selenite.colors: Colorless for selenite; gypsum in general ranges from clear and white to gray, yellow, red and brown.

septarian.name: Septarian
septarian.colors: Brown, tan, black, gray, white, reddish and golden. The three most common are brown, yellow and gray.

seraphinite.name: Seraphinite
seraphinite.colors: Usually dark green to gray with silvery shimmer. Rarely red, yellow, gold or black per S2.
seraphinite.chakra: Heart chakra especially, and all chakras per S2.

serpentine.name: Serpentine
serpentine.colors: Usually shades of green; also yellow, black, white and others.

shiva-lingam.name: Shiva Lingam
shiva-lingam.colors: Usually brown, light brown or beige, with stripes and patches of brown, red, tan and gray.
shiva-lingam.chakra: Said to tie to the whole chakra system, not a single chakra.

shungite.name: Shungite
shungite.colors: Black, gray or silver; may show golden or white veins or spots.

silver-sheen-obsidian.name: Silver Sheen Obsidian
silver-sheen-obsidian.colors: Obsidian is usually black; sheen specimens are named by the color of the sheen, such as silver, golden or rainbow.

smoky-quartz.name: Smoky Quartz
smoky-quartz.colors: Light yellowish brown to brown, so dark it can look black. Grayish brown is less desirable; orangish to reddish brown is preferred when cut.

snow-quartz.name: Snow Quartz
snow-quartz.colors: Milky white, various shades of white.

snowflake-obsidian.name: Snowflake Obsidian
snowflake-obsidian.colors: Black glass with white to gray radial clusters (snowflakes), giving a blotchy or snowflake pattern.

sodalite.name: Sodalite
sodalite.colors: Often bright blue to violet-blue with white veining; also gray, white, green, colorless, yellow, red.

spinel.name: Spinel
spinel.colors: Wide range: red, pink, orange, purple, blue, black. S3 says every spectrum color including green and yellow; S2 says pure green and yellow appear absent in nature.
spinel.birthstone: August birthstone since July 2016, alongside peridot (and sardonyx per S1).

spirit-quartz.name: Spirit Quartz
spirit-quartz.colors: Quartz in general occurs in virtually every color. No source gives the color of spirit quartz.

star-sapphire.name: Star Sapphire
star-sapphire.colors: Every color but red; red stones are star rubies. Black, pink and blue are the most common (S4).
star-sapphire.chakra: S4 says the range of colors means star sapphires can serve every chakra.

strawberry-quartz.name: Strawberry Quartz
strawberry-quartz.colors: Pinkish-red. Fine inclusions give a uniform strawberry shade; bolder ones show reddish needles, flakes or glints in clearer quartz.

sunstone.name: Sunstone
sunstone.colors: Colorless, yellow, orange and red, with some pink, green or blue stones. S1 lists yellow, green, red, red-brown, colorless.

tangerine-quartz.name: Tangerine Quartz
tangerine-quartz.colors: Citrine ranges from pale lemon yellow to rich orange or brown; S2 says quartz occurs in virtually every color.
tangerine-quartz.chakra: Citrine ties to the solar plexus chakra per S5.
tangerine-quartz.birthstone: Citrine is the November birthstone (citrine, not the named stone).

tanzanite.name: Tanzanite
tanzanite.colors: Violet blue to bluish violet to violet purple.

tektite.name: Tektite
aliases: Libyan desert glass (listed with tektites by S1)
tektite.colors: Black, green, brown or grey; moldavites and georgiaites are green, australites, indochinites and ivorites mostly black.

tiffany-stone.name: Tiffany Stone
tiffany-stone.colors: Purple, blue and white, sometimes with yellow, brown, pink or black patches.

tigers-eye.name: Tiger's Eye
tigers-eye.colors: Golden brown to red-brown; unstained pieces keep the original blue and are called Hawk's Eye; some pieces show both.

topaz.name: Topaz
topaz.colors: Colorless, yellow, orange, brown, red, pink, blue and green naturally. Most natural topaz is colorless.
topaz.birthstone: The original modern birthstone for November. Citrine was added as a second November stone in 1952.

tourmalinated-quartz.name: Tourmalinated Quartz
tourmalinated-quartz.colors: Listed as black, gray and multi-color; base quartz is usually colorless with black tourmaline.

tourmaline.name: Tourmaline
tourmaline.colors: Every spectrum color; black is most common. Crystals are often color-zoned.
tourmaline.birthstone: Birthstone for October per S2; Kunz 1913 doubted it belongs since it was only known from the 18th century.

tree-agate.name: Tree Agate
aliases: moss agate (S5 treats tree agate as a type of it)
tree-agate.colors: Tree agate is opaque white with green tree-like inclusions (S5).

trolleite.name: Trolleite
trolleite.colors: Light blue, light green; photos show pale or bluish trolleite.

turquoise.name: Turquoise
turquoise.colors: Blue to blue-green to yellowish green; sky or robin's-egg blue is most desirable, often with brown, gray or black matrix.
turquoise.birthstone: Traditional December birthstone; Kunz says it was also placed in other months in older lists.

turritella-agate.name: Turritella Agate
turritella-agate.colors: Brown agate with white-to-tan fossil snails standing out.

unakite.name: Unakite
unakite.colors: Pink and green, the pink and green colors make it a popular lapidary material.

vanadinite.name: Vanadinite
vanadinite.colors: Usually bright yellow, orange, red or brown; sometimes gray, black or colorless.

watermelon-tourmaline.name: Watermelon Tourmaline
watermelon-tourmaline.colors: Usually a green outer layer fading into a pink core; "reverse watermelon" has pink outside and a green core; rare blue tones occur.
watermelon-tourmaline.birthstone: Tourmaline in general is the October birthstone per S2.

white-calcite.name: White Calcite
white-calcite.colors: Usually white but also colorless, gray, red, green, blue, yellow, brown or orange.

white-jade.name: White Jade
white-jade.colors: Nephrite usually ranges from white through cream to dark green. Hetian stone runs creamy white to greenish, with pure white the most valuable.

white-opal.name: White Opal
white-opal.colors: White, yellow or cream body color; play of color can flash on top. White, gray and green are the most common opal body colors, black the rarest.
white-opal.birthstone: Opal in general is the October birthstone.

yellow-apatite.name: Yellow Apatite
yellow-apatite.colors: Apatite occurs in green, brown, blue, yellow, violet, pink and colorless. Yellow stones are one of these colors.

yellow-aventurine.name: Yellow Aventurine
yellow-aventurine.colors: Yellow is a less common aventurine color than green; yellow tumbling rough from India is pictured in S1.
yellow-aventurine.chakra: Sources conflict: S1 uses green aventurine for the heart chakra; S4 links aventurine to the brow and crown chakras. Neither is yellow-specific.

yellow-calcite.name: Yellow Calcite
yellow-calcite.colors: Calcite in general is usually white but also colorless, gray, red, green, blue, yellow, brown, orange. Yellow material noted as pale yellow (USSR) and light yellow (Bancroft, Ontario).

zebra-jasper.name: Zebra Jasper
zebra-jasper.colors: Brown and white stripes; one batch also included spotted pieces.

zircon.name: Zircon
zircon.colors: Usually yellow, brown or red; also colorless, gray, blue and green.

actinolite.name: Actinolite
actinolite.colors: Pale to dark green, yellowish green, blue and black; white or gray in asbestos form.

adamite.name: Adamite
adamite.colors: Pale yellow, honey-yellow, brownish yellow, reddish; rarely white, colorless, blue or green (S2). Also green, violet, pink and rose per S1.

afghanite.name: Afghanite
afghanite.colors: Blue to colorless, with light and dark blue shades (S1). S3 gives blue, and colorless in thin section.

african-turquoise.name: African Turquoise
african-turquoise.colors: Teal, green, black, brown and tan, in a mottled matrix of blues, greens, browns and blacks.

ammolite.name: Ammolite
ammolite.colors: Any spectral color is possible; red and green are most common, blue and purple less common, crimson, violet and gold very rare (S1). Base color is gray to brown (S2).

andalusite.name: Andalusite
andalusite.colors: Pink, violet, yellow, green, white and gray; greenish brown and yellowish green in S2's description; colorless in thin section.

apache-gold.name: Apache Gold
apache-gold.colors: Black schist with gleaming metallic grains. Chalcopyrite in general is brass yellow and tarnishes to gray green.

arfvedsonite.name: Arfvedsonite
arfvedsonite.colors: Black to greenish black, with deep green on thin edges; strongly pleochroic in blue-greens, yellow-browns and gray-violets.

auralite-23.name: Auralite 23
auralite-23.colors: Purple, red and greenish gray zones, sometimes a separate golden zone, seen along the threefold axis.

axinite.name: Axinite
axinite.colors: Strongly pleochroic: gems can show three colors depending on viewing angle; color zoning and color change are also reported (S1).

baltic-amber.name: Baltic Amber
baltic-amber.colors: Amber in general: yellow, orange and brown. Rare pieces can be green, blue or violet.
baltic-amber.birthstone: Amber is not a birthstone, per S1.

banded-agate.name: Banded Agate
banded-agate.colors: Wide range, including brown, white, red, gray, pink, black and yellow (S2). Banded agates show regular color layers and bright colors (S1).

barite.name: Barite
barite.colors: Colorless, white, light blue, yellow, red, green per S2; also grey and brown per S3. Colored crystals can show weak pleochroism per S1.

black-amethyst.name: Black Amethyst
black-amethyst.colors: Amethyst in general ranges from pale lilac to deep reddish purple (S2). Smoky quartz, not amethyst, is the quartz described as shades of black and brown (S7).
black-amethyst.birthstone: Amethyst in general is the February birthstone (GIA). Not stated for black amethyst.

black-jasper.name: Black Jasper
black-jasper.colors: Black is among the jasper colours listed. Basanite is described as deep velvety black. Blackstone shows cream-to-brown inclusions.

black-opal.name: Black Opal
black-opal.colors: Dark body color, often black or dark gray; can also be very dark bluish, greenish or brownish, per S2 and S3.
black-opal.birthstone: Opal (family) is an October birthstone, per S1.

black-quartz.name: Black Quartz
black-quartz.colors: Smoky quartz ranges from brown or smoky gray to a nearly opaque black (S4).

black-ruby.name: Black Ruby
black-ruby.colors: Ruby-level only: GIA lists red; Wikipedia lists orangy red through strongly purplish red. No source describes a black color for ruby.
black-ruby.birthstone: Ruby-level only: GIA says ruby is the July birthstone and the gem for the 15th and 40th anniversaries.

black-rutilated-quartz.name: Black Rutilated Quartz
black-rutilated-quartz.colors: Clear or colorless quartz with black needles. Rutile needles in general can be golden, silver, red or greenish; black ones may be rutile (S1) or tourmaline (S3).

black-sapphire.name: Black Sapphire
black-sapphire.colors: Black is one of several non-blue colors sapphire can take, along with gray, brown and colorless (S3, S1).
black-sapphire.birthstone: Sapphire in general is the September birthstone (parent S1); the sources do not say this applies to black sapphire.

black-spinel.name: Black Spinel
black-spinel.colors: Black is one spinel color; dark spinels that look black are also called ceylonite or pleonaste (S3).
black-spinel.birthstone: Spinel was named an August birthstone in July 2016 (S3).

blue-agate.name: Blue Agate
blue-agate.colors: Agate in general ranges from pale blue to black, red, yellow and more (Wikipedia). Holly Blue shows soft, hazy blue to blue-grey banding with white, cream or pale grey.

blue-amber.name: Blue Amber
blue-amber.colors: Blue amber shows a greenish blue surface color over a yellow to orange-brown body. Amber in general is yellow, orange and brown.

blue-jasper.name: Blue Jasper
blue-jasper.colors: Jasper in general: most commonly red, rarely blue (Wikipedia). GemSelect says blues and purples are not impossible. No source describes a blue shade.

blue-kyanite.name: Blue Kyanite
blue-kyanite.colors: Most gem kyanite is blue, but it can also be clear, green, black and rarely purple (S2). Blue kyanite can range from clear to dark blue (S2).
blue-kyanite.birthstone: Not a traditional birthstone for any month (S5).

blue-moonstone.name: Blue Moonstone
blue-moonstone.colors: Blue sheen on colorless feldspar; moonstone bodycolors include white, gray, brown, pink, orange, green and yellow (family, per S3).
blue-moonstone.birthstone: June birthstone, sharing the title with pearls and alexandrite (moonstone family, per S3).

blue-obsidian.name: Blue Obsidian
blue-obsidian.colors: Blue is rare; obsidian is usually black, sometimes brown, tan or green (parent-level); no blue-specific shade is described

blue-quartz.name: Blue Quartz
blue-quartz.colors: Blue to violet for dumortierite quartz. Quartz in general occurs in many colors, including blue (parent level).

blue-quartzite.name: Blue Quartzite
blue-quartzite.colors: Quartzite in general is usually white to gray; impurities can make it blue (geology.com). Azul Macaubas shows light blue, cyan and indigo shades (dealer).

blue-topaz.name: Blue Topaz
blue-topaz.colors: Sold from pale to deep blue; Swiss Blue is lighter and London Blue darker (S2).
blue-topaz.birthstone: The November birthstone is orange (precious) topaz, not blue topaz, per S3 (parent-level).

blue-tourmaline.name: Blue Tourmaline
blue-tourmaline.colors: Blue ranges from light blue to bluish-green (elbaite) to intense neon blue (paraíba) (per S3, S1).

blue-turquoise.name: Blue Turquoise
blue-turquoise.colors: Sky or robin's-egg blue is the most desirable (S3). Turquoise also ranges from blue-green to yellowish green (S2, S3).
blue-turquoise.birthstone: Turquoise is the traditional birthstone for December, and also for people born on Saturday (S1, S3).

blue-zircon.name: Blue Zircon
blue-zircon.colors: Natural zircon is usually yellow, brown or red; blue is mostly produced by heat treatment.
blue-zircon.birthstone: Modern birthstone for December, alongside blue topaz and tanzanite (S2, S4).

bolivianite.name: Bolivianite
bolivianite.colors: Purple and yellow-orange in alternating zones within one crystal.

boulder-opal.name: Boulder Opal
boulder-opal.colors: Many colors with dazzling fire over brown ironstone, per S2; opal in general spans many colors, per S4.
boulder-opal.birthstone: October birthstone for opal in general, per S1 and S2.

bronzite.name: Bronzite
bronzite.colors: Green or brown per S1; S3 says mostly brown to black with scattered gold speckles from fibrous inclusions.
bronzite.chakra: Enstatite (parent), per a dealer page, is used to align all seven chakras, emphasizing the sacral chakra. Not stated for bronzite.
bronzite.birthstone: Enstatite (parent) is not a birthstone; only green chrome-enstatite substitutes for emerald as a May stone. Nothing for bronzite.

brookite.name: Brookite
brookite.colors: Deep red, reddish brown, yellowish brown, brown or black; dark brown to iron-black in most material.

caribbean-calcite.name: Caribbean Calcite
caribbean-calcite.colors: Turquoise per dealer S4. Calcite in general is white or colorless, with many other colors from impurities (parent S2).

cassiterite.name: Cassiterite
cassiterite.colors: Black, brownish black, reddish brown, brown, red, yellow, gray, white; rarely colorless. Most crystals are dark.

cerussite.name: Cerussite
cerussite.colors: Usually colorless or white, sometimes grey or greenish; yellow and green also occur (S1, S2).

chalcedony.name: Chalcedony
chalcedony.colors: Most commonly white to gray, grayish-blue or brown; varieties add red, orange, green and purple (S1, S2).

chalcocite.name: Chalcocite
chalcocite.colors: Dark gray to black, per S1.

chicken-blood-stone.name: Chicken Blood Stone
chicken-blood-stone.colors: Eight basic colors blending in layers: red, black, white, yellow, green, blue, gray, purple. Some specimens are entirely red.

chrome-diopside.name: Chrome Diopside
chrome-diopside.colors: Bright green to emerald green, with a deep green color from chromium (S4, S1).

chrysanthemum-stone.name: Chrysanthemum Stone
chrysanthemum-stone.colors: Dark grey to black base with milky white, flower-shaped crystals, per S1.

cobalto-calcite.name: Cobalto Calcite
cobalto-calcite.colors: Pink, from pinkish-salmon to hot pink (S5); S6 lists pink, rose, magenta and lavender.
cobalto-calcite.chakra: Heart chakra, per a dealer page; it says this is cultural and traditional, not scientific.

cuprite.name: Cuprite
cuprite.colors: Dark red to cochineal red, sometimes almost black, per S2 infobox.

dallasite.name: Dallasite
dallasite.colors: Thin rectangular chunks of green or brown lava set in a silicified matrix, per S2.

dark-amber.name: Dark Amber
dark-amber.colors: Mostly yellow, orange and brown (parent-level). Green, blue or violet tints are rare. Dark brown or red-brown tones are described for aged natural pieces.
dark-amber.birthstone: Amber is not a birthstone, per GIA.

dendritic-agate.name: Dendritic Agate
dendritic-agate.colors: Whitish-gray or colorless ground with black, brown or green dendrites, per S6 and S4.

dendritic-opal.name: Dendritic Opal
dendritic-opal.colors: Body usually white, yellow, blue, green or pink with black inclusions, per S5. Host opal ranges from milky white to brown, per S6.
dendritic-opal.birthstone: October birthstone, per S1 (opal family, parent-level).

diopside.name: Diopside
diopside.colors: Commonly light to dark green; may be blue, brown, colorless, white, grey, pale violet (S3). Violane is light blue to purple (S5).

dioptase.name: Dioptase
dioptase.colors: Intense emerald-green to bluish-green (S2); S1 calls the color emerald-like.

double-terminated-quartz.name: Double Terminated Quartz
double-terminated-quartz.colors: Herkimer diamonds range from colorless to smoky gray or black. Quartz in general occurs in nearly every color.

dragonstone.name: Dragonstone
dragonstone.colors: Greens, reds, brown, grey per Fire Mountain Gems; green matrix with red per FossilEra.
dragonstone.chakra: Heart Chakra per Fire Mountain Gems (metaphysical).

dumortierite.name: Dumortierite
dumortierite.colors: Brown, blue and green are most common; violet and pink are rarer.

enhydro-quartz.name: Enhydro Quartz
enhydro-quartz.colors: Usually colorless in the trade. GIA also describes enhydro amethyst from Morocco with a rich reddish purple hue.

ethiopian-opal.name: Ethiopian Opal
ethiopian-opal.colors: Welo opal has clear, white, yellow, orange, or brown body colors with vivid play-of-color, per S3.
ethiopian-opal.birthstone: Opal is an October birthstone, per GIA (parent opal).

euclase.name: Euclase
euclase.colors: Mostly colorless or white; blue to green and yellowish green; rare pink-orange from Brazil, per S2.

eudialyte.name: Eudialyte
eudialyte.colors: Deep to bright red is typical for gem material; other sources list magenta, brown, blue and yellow.

fire-quartz.name: Fire Quartz
fire-quartz.colors: Quartz occurs in virtually every color (parent level); fire-related colors are not described in any source.

flint.name: Flint
flint.colors: Flint can be sandy brown, medium to dark grey, black, reddish brown or off-white grey, per S2.

fuchsite.name: Fuchsite
fuchsite.colors: Light green to emerald green, depending on chromium content.

garden-quartz.name: Garden Quartz
garden-quartz.colors: Quartz in general occurs in virtually every color, per S2. Garden quartz color is not covered by any source.

gilsonite.name: Gilsonite
gilsonite.colors: Black, per S2 (resembles shiny black obsidian); used in dark-colored printing inks and paints (S2).

goethite.name: Goethite
goethite.colors: Yellowish to reddish to dark brown or black.

goshenite.name: Goshenite
goshenite.colors: Colorless to near-colorless (S2). S5 says white goshenite is usually opaque.

grandidierite.name: Grandidierite
grandidierite.colors: Cyan to turquoise, bluish green; can be dark blue-green, colorless or dark green depending on the angle.

green-agate.name: Green Agate
green-agate.colors: Agate is often multicolored and rarely green (S3). S4 lists green among natural agate colours.

green-amber.name: Green Amber
green-amber.colors: Amber is usually yellow, orange and brown (S1); green amber is rare, and green tints occur in rare pieces (S1, S2).

green-beryl.name: Green Beryl
green-beryl.colors: Light green (S2). Beryl colors in general include green, blue, yellow, pink and red (S3, parent).
green-beryl.birthstone: Kunz (1913) proposed beryl as an October birthstone, not a modern birthstone list.

green-fluorite.name: Green Fluorite
green-fluorite.colors: Green is a typical fluorite color (S2). Chrome green from Colombia is described as rare (S1). Fluorite also comes in purple, blue, yellow and colorless (S1, S2).

green-garnet.name: Green Garnet
green-garnet.colors: Tsavorite is various shades of green (S5); andradite runs yellow-green to green (S2); uvarovite is dark green (S2).
green-garnet.birthstone: Garnet (parent) is the birthstone for January (S1); green garnet is not named separately.

green-jasper.name: Green Jasper
green-jasper.colors: Jasper is most commonly red, but may be yellow, brown, green or rarely blue (S2). Green jasper is light to dark green (S3).
green-jasper.chakra: Vividly green jasper may link to the Heart chakra (S4).
green-jasper.birthstone: Bloodstone, a jasper variety, is the March birthstone (S4). Jasper is a mystical birthstone for October (S4). Green jasper is not named directly.

green-moss-agate.name: Green Moss Agate
green-moss-agate.colors: Colorless to white, translucent, with green veins; sometimes brown and red inclusions.

green-onyx.name: Green Onyx
green-onyx.colors: Onyx is black and white banded, and sardonyx is red to brown with black or white. Green onyx is usually dyed green chalcedony, and chrysoprase is apple green chalcedony.
green-onyx.chakra: A seller article links chalcedony color to chakras. In that belief system, green is the Heart chakra.

green-sapphire.name: Green Sapphire
green-sapphire.colors: Green is one of the fancy sapphire colors, which also include violet, yellow, orange, pink and purple (S1, S3). Blue is the typical sapphire color.
green-sapphire.birthstone: Sapphire is the birthstone for September (S1). Green sapphire is not separately covered.

green-tourmaline.name: Green Tourmaline
green-tourmaline.colors: Green tourmaline is dark green, sometimes light green or light brown. Tourmaline in general occurs in many colors.
green-tourmaline.birthstone: Tourmaline in general is the birthstone for October (parent level).

green-turquoise.name: Green Turquoise
green-turquoise.colors: Blue to green in the source's color listing (per S1); green and yellowish green tints are less desirable than blue (per S3).
green-turquoise.birthstone: Turquoise is the traditional December birthstone, and also the birthstone for those born on Saturday (per S1 and S2).

grossular.name: Grossular
grossular.colors: Very wide range: yellow-green, pale to dark green, golden yellow, pink, red, orange, brownish red, colorless, white, gray, black.

hackmanite.name: Hackmanite
hackmanite.colors: Usually pink to violet, fading to greenish-white or gray in sunlight (S3). Freshly quarried pieces are generally pale to deep violet (S1).
hackmanite.chakra: Purple to violet hackmanites are called crown chakra stones, per S3 (modern lore).
hackmanite.birthstone: Not a traditional birthstone, but it can stand in for amethyst (February) or lapis lazuli (September), per S3.

halite.name: Halite
halite.colors: Colorless or white when pure. Impurities give yellow, gray, black, brown, red and other colors. Some halite is light or dark blue, purple, pink.

heliodor.name: Heliodor
heliodor.colors: Yellow, greenish yellow to golden-yellow (S2). S1 says greenish yellow is heliodor and pure yellow to gold is golden beryl, though some references do not separate them.

hessonite.name: Hessonite
hessonite.colors: Orange, ranging from honey yellow to reddish-brown; sometimes pinkish; Wikipedia describes red inclining to orange or yellow
hessonite.birthstone: Garnet is the January birthstone at the garnet-group level (GIA); hessonite is not named separately

honey-calcite.name: Honey Calcite
honey-calcite.colors: Pure calcite is colorless or white. When colored crystals are found, they are generally yellow to honey-colored, per S5.

honeycomb-calcite.name: Honeycomb Calcite
honeycomb-calcite.colors: Calcite in general is white or colorless; impurities can give gray, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet, brown or black.

hyalite-opal.name: Hyalite Opal
hyalite-opal.colors: Colorless or white body (per S2); under UV it glows strong green to yellow-green (per S5).
hyalite-opal.birthstone: Opal is an October birthstone (opal family, per S1); the sources do not name hyalite separately.

indian-agate.name: Indian Agate
indian-agate.colors: Agate in general occurs in brown, white, red, gray, pink, black and yellow (S2); S3 adds blue, orange, purple and green rarely.

iris-agate.name: Iris Agate
iris-agate.colors: Base color light grey to brown; iridescent colors include blue, green, purple and yellow (per S5).

jet.name: Jet
jet.colors: Black, or dark brown; may contain brassy pyrite inclusions per Wikipedia

kingman-turquoise.name: Kingman Turquoise
kingman-turquoise.colors: Medium to dark blue with pyrite flecks; bright blue with black spider-web matrix per S3. Turquoise overall runs blue to green.
kingman-turquoise.birthstone: Turquoise is the traditional birthstone for December, per S1. S2 notes it is also the birthstone for those born on Saturday.

kiwi-jasper.name: Kiwi Jasper
kiwi-jasper.colors: Light green or sea green with black and white flecks, per S3.
kiwi-jasper.chakra: Heart chakra, per the dealer blog (S3). A metaphysical claim, not a fact.

lace-agate.name: Lace Agate
aliases: Crazy Lace agate (Mexican lace agate, separate variety)
lace-agate.colors: Overall pale or light blue, layered with white in wavy lace-like bands.

laguna-agate.name: Laguna Agate
laguna-agate.colors: Laguna hues run from reds and oranges to yellows, pinks and purples, framed by whites and grays, per S4. Agate in general comes in many colors, per S2.

lazurite.name: Lazurite
lazurite.colors: Deep blue, azure, violet-blue and greenish blue, per S1 infobox.

lepidocrocite.name: Lepidocrocite
lepidocrocite.colors: Ruby-red to reddish brown; light reddish to red-orange in transmitted light; gray-white in reflected light. Streak conflicts: Wikipedia text says yellow-brown, handbook says dull orange

libyan-desert-glass.name: Libyan Desert Glass
libyan-desert-glass.colors: Canary yellow to yellow-green, per S4 and S1.

london-blue-topaz.name: London Blue Topaz
london-blue-topaz.colors: London blue is a deep blue (S4). Topaz in general occurs in many natural colors (S2).
london-blue-topaz.birthstone: Topaz is the modern birthstone for November (parent family, S2).

magnetite.name: Magnetite
magnetite.colors: Black to silvery gray per S1; black or gray with a brownish tint in reflected sun per S2.

mammoth-ivory.name: Mammoth Ivory
mammoth-ivory.colors: Usually brown on the surface; occasionally blue to dark blue or even black (S1).

merlinite.name: Merlinite
merlinite.colors: Black dendrites on a translucent or white background (S3). The host chalcedony is most often white to gray, grayish-blue or brown (S2).
merlinite.chakra: A dealer guide links Mystic Merlinite (Indigo Gabbro) to chakra balancing. No source covers dendritic merlinite (S4).

milky-quartz.name: Milky Quartz
milky-quartz.colors: White, various shades usually milky (S4); the cloudy look is what gives the variety its name.

moissanite.name: Moissanite
moissanite.colors: Colors vary widely, graded from D to K on the diamond color grading scale, per S1.

moqui-marbles.name: Moqui Marbles
moqui-marbles.colors: Almost black or brownish-black, with a pitted surface polished by blowing sand.

mystic-topaz.name: Mystic Topaz
mystic-topaz.colors: The rainbow colors come from the coating; the base is colorless topaz, and the coating shifts from green through blue, violet, magenta and orange (S5).
mystic-topaz.birthstone: Topaz is the original modern birthstone for November (parent S2); the sources do not name mystic topaz as one.

natrolite.name: Natrolite
natrolite.colors: Colorless or white, sometimes gray, yellowish or reddish per S1. The Wikipedia infobox adds sometimes pink.

ocean-picture-stone.name: Ocean Picture Stone
ocean-picture-stone.colors: Vibrant colours with striking patterns, per S2.

orange-sapphire.name: Orange Sapphire
orange-sapphire.colors: Fancy sapphires, including orange, come in yellow, orange, green, brown, purple, violet and practically any other hue (sapphire family, per S3).
orange-sapphire.birthstone: Sapphire is the September birthstone; the sources do not name orange sapphire separately.

orbicular-jasper.name: Orbicular Jasper
orbicular-jasper.colors: Jasper in general is most commonly red, per S2. Ocean jasper, a related trade name, has a multicolored background of green, yellow, pink and more, per S4.

orthoceras.name: Orthoceras
orthoceras.colors: Fossil shows as chambers in white calcite inside a red, pink or grey limestone matrix in the museum specimen (S2).

orthoclase.name: Orthoclase
orthoclase.colors: White, gray, pink, reddish, yellow, green or colorless; yellow gem material is common from Madagascar.

peacock-ore.name: Peacock Ore
peacock-ore.colors: Reddish brown on a fresh surface; brown to black with purplish-bluish tarnish (S1, S2).

persian-turquoise.name: Persian Turquoise
persian-turquoise.colors: Sky blue or robin's-egg blue is the most prized color, with little or no green. Turquoise in general also ranges to bluish green and green.
persian-turquoise.birthstone: Turquoise is the traditional birthstone for December (parent-level).

phenakite.name: Phenakite
phenakite.colors: Colorless, pale yellow, pink, brown; rare red gems come from Russian material.

phosphosiderite.name: Phosphosiderite
phosphosiderite.colors: Usually red, pink or purple, sometimes green, with yellow veining. Often bright orchid-purple with yellow streaks. Can also be colorless.

picasso-jasper.name: Picasso Jasper
picasso-jasper.colors: Picasso jasper shows abstract black, grey, brown and cream patterns (S3). Jasper in general is most often red, yellow, brown, green, rarely blue (S2).

picture-jasper.name: Picture Jasper
picture-jasper.colors: Jasper in general is most commonly red, also yellow, brown, green or rarely blue. Picture jasper is known for its patterns.

pink-agate.name: Pink Agate
pink-agate.colors: Agate in general includes pink among its natural colors (S2, S3). Intense, uniform pink is described as essentially unknown in untreated agate (S7).

pink-amethyst.name: Pink Amethyst
pink-amethyst.colors: Lilac to deep reddish purple (S2). Pinkish violet 'Rose de France' is the lightest shade (S2, S4). Most valued is strong reddish purple (S1).
pink-amethyst.birthstone: Amethyst is the birthstone of February (parent level, applies to amethyst in general).

pink-calcite.name: Pink Calcite
pink-calcite.colors: Usually white; also colorless, gray, red, green, blue, yellow, brown, orange (parent calcite). Pink is seen in marble from Tate, Georgia (S2).

pink-sapphire.name: Pink Sapphire
pink-sapphire.colors: Sapphire comes in every color but red. Pink sapphires range from light to dark pink and deepen with more chromium.
pink-sapphire.birthstone: Sapphire is the birthstone for September. The sources do not give a separate pink sapphire birthstone.

pink-topaz.name: Pink Topaz
pink-topaz.colors: Topaz occurs in natural colors including pink. Pink is one of the most highly regarded colors (S2).
pink-topaz.birthstone: Topaz is the original modern birthstone for November (S2). Citrine was added as a second November birthstone in 1952.

polychrome-jasper.name: Polychrome Jasper
polychrome-jasper.colors: Jasper can be almost any shade, but usually reds, browns, oranges, yellows and greens. Two, three or more hues often mingle on one stone (S4).
polychrome-jasper.chakra: Jasper often links to the Root Chakra. Vivid yellow or green jasper may point to the Solar Plexus or Heart chakras instead (S4).
polychrome-jasper.birthstone: Bloodstone, a type of jasper, is the March birthstone. Jasper is also called a mystical October birthstone (S4). Polychrome jasper has no birthstone of its own in the sources.

prophecy-stone.name: Prophecy Stone
prophecy-stone.colors: Goethite in general is blackish brown or yellowish, per S4.
prophecy-stone.chakra: Seller S6 assigns it to the Earth Star, Third Eye, Crown and Soul Star chakras.

purple-fluorite.name: Purple Fluorite
purple-fluorite.colors: Purple, often light to dark shades (S4). Fluorite is typically purple, green and yellow, and can also be colorless, blue, red or black (S2).

purple-opal.name: Purple Opal
purple-opal.colors: Parent-level: colorless, white, yellow, red, orange, green, brown, black, blue, pink. Purple is not listed for opal in general, but precious opal can flash purple.

purple-sapphire.name: Purple Sapphire
purple-sapphire.colors: Pinkish-lilac to deep violet, from soft lilac tones to plums and violets, per S5.
purple-sapphire.chakra: Crown chakra stone in the crystal healing tradition, per S5.
purple-sapphire.birthstone: September birthstone, per S1 and S5.

purple-turquoise.name: Purple Turquoise
purple-turquoise.colors: Natural turquoise runs blue to green, with white to powder blue also noted. IGS (parent) mentions rare blue-violet specimens with strontium; S8 says no natural purple turquoise exists.

purpurite.name: Purpurite
purpurite.colors: Reddish purple to deep rose-red; often darkened to brown or black at the surface by alteration.

pyromorphite.name: Pyromorphite
pyromorphite.colors: Usually bright green, yellow or brown; also orange, tan, grayish, white or colorless.

quartz-geode.name: Quartz Geode
quartz-geode.colors: Crystal colors vary with trace elements: iron gives red or purple, titanium blue, nickel or chromium green, manganese pink (geode crystals in general).

rainbow-obsidian.name: Rainbow Obsidian
rainbow-obsidian.colors: Multicolored iridescent bands in various colors (S4). Blue, green, purple and bronze are named (S5).

rainbow-quartz.name: Rainbow Quartz
rainbow-quartz.colors: A shifting rainbow effect and iridescent metallic sheen. GemSelect lists deep blues, purples, reds and greens on mystic quartz.
rainbow-quartz.chakra: Quartz in general: GemSelect says Hindu traditions link it to the crown chakra. Not specific to rainbow quartz.

realgar.name: Realgar
realgar.colors: Rich red to orange-red; it turns yellowish-orange (pararealgar) after exposure to light.

red-agate.name: Red Agate
red-agate.colors: Agate is often multicolored, with red to orange among its colours (S3). S4 lists red and reddish brown as natural colours.

red-coral.name: Red Coral
red-coral.colors: Deep red to soft pink per S3; S4 lists a range that includes red, pink, white and black for coral in general.

red-quartz.name: Red Quartz
red-quartz.colors: Quartz comes in many colors; S2 lists red among its common colors (parent-level).

red-spinel.name: Red Spinel
red-spinel.colors: Red, from bright red to vivid pink and orange. Spinel in general also comes in blue, purple, black and more (S1, S3).
red-spinel.birthstone: Spinel, including red spinel, is an August birthstone, added in 2016 (per S1, S2, S3).

red-tiger-eye.name: Red Tiger Eye
red-tiger-eye.colors: Golden to red-brown; red stones are usually developed by gentle heat treatment.

red-tourmaline.name: Red Tourmaline
red-tourmaline.colors: Red tourmaline (rubellite) shows reasonably saturated dark pink to red, often with purplish, orangish or brownish secondary hues (S1).
red-tourmaline.birthstone: Tourmaline is the October birthstone (S2); the sources do not say red tourmaline specifically.

roman-glass.name: Roman Glass
roman-glass.colors: Pale green tints, colorless, royal blue, dark blue and purple appear on the museum pieces; makers also used marbled, lace, striped and spiral patterns.

rubellite.name: Rubellite
rubellite.colors: Dark pink to red; light pink stones are more properly called pink tourmaline (S1).
rubellite.birthstone: Rubellite is called the modern October birthstone (S1); tourmaline serves as October birthstone (parent S2).

rudraksha.name: Rudraksha
rudraksha.colors: The ripe fruit is blue (structural colour, not pigment); the bead stone itself has no colour stated in the sources.

rutilated-quartz.name: Rutilated Quartz
rutilated-quartz.colors: Mainly colorless, transparent quartz with golden, red, or near-black rutile needles; a smoky brown form is less common (S5, S6).

scheelite.name: Scheelite
scheelite.colors: Colorless, white, gray, brown, golden yellow, orange, red and green.

shattuckite.name: Shattuckite
shattuckite.colors: Blue: dark and light blue, turquoise per S2; deep to medium blue per S4. Strongly pleochroic from very pale to deep blue.

siderite.name: Siderite
siderite.colors: Pale yellow to tan, grey, brown, green, red, black, sometimes nearly colorless (S2). Golden and honey-colored gems are the prized ones (S1).

spessartine.name: Spessartine
spessartine.colors: Yellow through red, per S1; violet-red forms are found in rhyolites in Colorado and Maine.

sphalerite.name: Sphalerite
sphalerite.colors: Many colors: brown, orange, yellow, green, red, whitish gray and black; colorless is very rare (S1).

spiny-oyster.name: Spiny Oyster
spiny-oyster.colors: Species vary considerably in appearance; live animals have colourful mantle edges.

star-garnet.name: Star Garnet
star-garnet.colors: Deep brownish-red to reddish-black per GemSelect (S6); purplish-red to chocolatey brownish-red per the Idaho dealer page (S8).
star-garnet.birthstone: Garnet in general is the January birthstone, per GIA. Not specific to star garnet.

star-ruby.name: Star Ruby
star-ruby.colors: Orangy red through strongly purplish red per S3 (parent); fine gems are a pure, vibrant red to slightly purplish red per S1.
star-ruby.birthstone: July birthstone, per S1 (ruby family, parent-level).

stichtite.name: Stichtite
stichtite.colors: Ranges from pink through lilac to a rich purple.

stilbite.name: Stilbite
stilbite.colors: Usually colorless or white, also yellow, brown, pink, salmon, orange, red, green, blue or black.

sugilite.name: Sugilite
sugilite.colors: Gem-quality pink to reddish purple to purple; impure material yellow, brown or black.

super-seven.name: Super Seven
super-seven.colors: GemRock (dealer, French) says generally multicolored, most often purple-dominant from amethyst, with brown, black, yellow, orange or red accents.
super-seven.chakra: GemRock (dealer, French) says the seven stones are claimed to balance and align all seven chakras. This is a metaphysical claim.
super-seven.birthstone: GemRock (dealer, French) says super seven is not a birthstone itself, but amethyst (February) and clear quartz (April alternative) are among its components.

taaffeite.name: Taaffeite
taaffeite.colors: Pink and purple shades (lilac, violet, mauve), also red, brown, bluish, gray, green or colorless per National Jeweler.

thomsonite.name: Thomsonite
thomsonite.colors: Colorless, white, beige or pink; sometimes green, yellow or red.

titanium-quartz.name: Titanium Quartz
titanium-quartz.colors: Iridescence shows the whole rainbow, usually blue, purple and green shades dominant. Coating metal changes the color.
titanium-quartz.chakra: S6 says it aligns and balances all seven chakras (dealer claim).
titanium-quartz.birthstone: S6 calls mystic quartz an April birthstone and a substitute for amethyst as February birthstone (dealer claim).

tsavorite-garnet.name: Tsavorite Garnet
tsavorite-garnet.colors: Tsavorite is a bright green (S3); grossular occurs in greens, yellows, pinks and more (S2).
tsavorite-garnet.birthstone: Garnet is the January birthstone for the parent garnet group, per GIA; no source gives a tsavorite-specific birthstone.

variscite.name: Variscite
variscite.colors: Typically yellowish green to bluish green, often with yellow, brown or black matrix; rarely red or violet.

vesuvianite.name: Vesuvianite
vesuvianite.colors: Mostly green, yellowish green or brownish green; rare colorless, white, blue, pink, purple, violet, red or black; often zoned.

vivianite.name: Vivianite
vivianite.colors: Colorless to very pale green when unaltered; oxidizes to blue, then darker green, brown, purple or black (per S2).

white-agate.name: White Agate
white-agate.colors: Agate colors include brown, white, red, gray, pink, black and yellow (parent-level). No source describes white agate on its own.

white-onyx.name: White Onyx
white-onyx.colors: Onyx marble bands run from pure white through honey, amber, green and brown (S2). Chalcedony onyx is typically black and white, sardonyx red to brown (S1).

white-sapphire.name: White Sapphire
white-sapphire.colors: Colorless to white, often slightly cloudy; natural colorless stones are rare (S4).
white-sapphire.birthstone: Sapphire in general is the September birthstone (S1); the sources do not say this applies to white sapphire.

white-topaz.name: White Topaz
white-topaz.colors: Colourless is the most common natural colour of topaz (S2), so white topaz is the colourless form (S5, S2).
white-topaz.birthstone: Topaz is the November birthstone (S2, S3). S5 gives blue topaz for December. No source names white topaz as a birthstone.

white-turquoise.name: White Turquoise
white-turquoise.colors: Blue to blue-green to yellowish green (parent-level). Wikipedia says the color can range from white to powder blue to sky blue, which conflicts with IGS on white.
white-turquoise.birthstone: Turquoise is the traditional birthstone for December (parent-level).

willemite.name: Willemite
willemite.colors: Most faceted willemites are pale green, yellow-orange or brownish green; blue is rare, from Quebec and Namibia (S1). Occurs in many colors in daylight (S2).

wulfenite.name: Wulfenite
wulfenite.colors: Bright yellow, yellow-orange, bright orange, red-orange and bright red; also gray, white, colorless, green, blue, brown and black per S4.

yellow-agate.name: Yellow Agate
yellow-agate.colors: Agate colors include yellow, along with brown, white, red, gray, pink and black (agate-level; yellow agate is not named separately).

yellow-jade.name: Yellow Jade
yellow-jade.colors: Jade occurs in many colors, including yellow (S1). Yellow occurs in jadeite and in nephrite (S2).

yellow-jasper.name: Yellow Jasper
yellow-jasper.colors: Yellow is one of the usual jasper colors, with red most common; yellow jasper is often brecciated (S2, S3, S1).
yellow-jasper.chakra: Metaphysical sources say vivid yellow jasper might sway the Solar Plexus or Heart chakras (S4).
yellow-jasper.birthstone: Jasper is listed as a mystical birthstone for October (S4, parent); yellow jasper is not named separately.

yellow-opal.name: Yellow Opal
yellow-opal.colors: Opal comes in many body colors. Yellow is one; iron opals are red to yellow, and fire opals have a yellow, orange or red body color.

yellow-sapphire.name: Yellow Sapphire
yellow-sapphire.colors: Fancy sapphires come in yellow, orange, green, brown, purple and other hues. Strong, vivid saturation is preferred.
yellow-sapphire.birthstone: Sapphire is the birthstone for September (sapphire family, parent level).

yellow-topaz.name: Yellow Topaz
yellow-topaz.colors: Yellow topaz ranges from golden yellow to reddish-orange; topaz in general also occurs in colorless, pale yellow, brown, pink, blue.
yellow-topaz.birthstone: Yellow topaz is a modern November birthstone; topaz in all colors is also considered the traditional one.

yttrium-fluorite.name: Yttrium Fluorite
yttrium-fluorite.colors: Fluorite in general is typically purple, green and yellow, also colorless, blue, red and black. No color is given for yttrofluorite itself; the photo caption only calls the specimen light.

zoisite.name: Zoisite
zoisite.colors: Colorless, gray, yellow, brown, pink, green, blue and violet. Tanzanite is blue to violet; thulite is pink.

aegirine.name: Aegirine
aegirine.colors: Dark green to greenish black, also reddish brown or black.

alabandite.name: Alabandite
alabandite.colors: Iron-black, tarnishing brown, deep green to brown and red in thin slivers.

albite.name: Albite
albite.colors: White to gray, bluish, greenish or reddish, sometimes chatoyant.

allophane.name: Allophane
allophane.colors: White, pale blue to sky blue, green or brown.

almandine.name: Almandine
almandine.colors: Deep red, brownish red, red-violet or black, sometimes sectored.

alunite.name: Alunite
alunite.colors: Colorless if pure, otherwise white, pale gray, yellow, red or reddish brown.

amblygonite.name: Amblygonite
amblygonite.colors: Milk-white, pale yellow, beige, salmon-pink, pale green, pale blue, gray, or colorless.

ametrine.name: Ametrine
ametrine.colors: Bicolor orange or yellow and purple.

analcime.name: Analcime
analcime.colors: White, colorless, gray, pink, greenish or yellowish.

anapaite.name: Anapaite
anapaite.colors: Green to pale green, colorless to pale green in transmitted light.

anatase.name: Anatase
anatase.colors: Brown, pale yellow or reddish brown, indigo, black, also pale green, pale lilac and gray.

andesine.name: Andesine
andesine.colors: White, gray, green and yellow as natural mineral.

andradite.name: Andradite
andradite.colors: Green, yellowish green, yellow, brown, brownish red and black.

anglesite.name: Anglesite
anglesite.colors: Colorless to white, commonly tinted gray, also orange, yellow, green, blue and rarely violet.

anhydrite.name: Anhydrite
anhydrite.colors: Colorless, white and light shades of brown, red, gray, pink, blue and violet.

anorthite.name: Anorthite
anorthite.colors: White, grayish and reddish, colorless in thin section.

anorthoclase.name: Anorthoclase
anorthoclase.colors: Colorless, also white, pale creamy yellow, red and green.

anthophyllite.name: Anthophyllite
anthophyllite.colors: Gray, brownish gray, yellowish brown, clove-brown, brownish green and emerald-green.

antlerite.name: Antlerite
antlerite.colors: Emerald-green, blackish green and pale green.

apricot-agate.name: Apricot Agate
apricot-agate.colors: A blend of white, yellow, pink, peach and orange.

arsenopyrite.name: Arsenopyrite
arsenopyrite.colors: Silvery-white to steel gray, tarnishing to pink, brown or copper tones.

astrophyllite.name: Astrophyllite
astrophyllite.colors: Bronze yellow to gold yellow, brown to reddish brown.

atacamite.name: Atacamite
atacamite.colors: Bright green, dark emerald-green to blackish green.

aurichalcite.name: Aurichalcite
aurichalcite.colors: Pale green, greenish blue and sky blue.

autunite.name: Autunite
autunite.colors: Lemon-yellow to sulfur-yellow, greenish yellow to pale green, sometimes dark green to greenish black.

aventurine.name: Aventurine Stone,
aventurine.colors: Most often green, but also orange, yellow, red, pink, brown, white, gray and blue.

banded-amethyst.name: Banded Amethyst
banded-amethyst.colors: Purple amethyst bands with white milky quartz and gray smoky quartz. Zones run from dark purple to light purple and white.
banded-amethyst.birthstone: Amethyst in general is the birthstone for February.

bauxite.name: Bauxite
bauxite.colors: White, gray, sometimes stained yellow, orange, red, pink or brown by iron.

benitoite.name: Benitoite
benitoite.colors: Mostly violetish-blue, sometimes colorless, with rare orange heat-treated stones.

beryl.name: Beryl
beryl.colors: Green, yellow, blue, red, pink, orange or colorless, normally colorless when pure.

bismuth.name: Bismuth
bismuth.colors: Silver-white with a reddish hue, tarnishing yellow to dark gray or iridescent.

bismuthinite.name: Bismuthinite
bismuthinite.colors: Lead-gray to tin-white, with a yellowish or iridescent tarnish.

black-diamond.name: Black Diamond
black-diamond.colors: Black, though the diamond itself may be nearly colorless, brown or very dark green.

black-mica.name: Black Mica
black-mica.colors: Black, dark green or dark brown.

black-star-diopside.name: Black Star Diopside
black-star-diopside.colors: Natural black, with a thin white or silver star on a jet-black stone.

black-star-sapphire.name: Black Star Sapphire
black-star-sapphire.colors: Black, from sapphire so dark that light barely passes through, whatever its underlying hue.

blue-diamond.name: Blue Diamond
blue-diamond.colors: Mostly grey with a tint of blue, with saturation ranging from fancy to fancy vivid.

blue-halite.name: Blue Halite
blue-halite.colors: Blue, from blue to deep blue.

blue-john-fluorite.name: Blue John Fluorite
blue-john-fluorite.colors: Streaked or banded zones of dark blue and violet with lighter yellowish, greenish or off-white zones.

blue-spinel.name: Blue Spinel
blue-spinel.colors: Many shades of blue, from darker greenish blue to vivid, intense blue.

boleite.name: Boleite
boleite.colors: Deep Prussian blue to indigo, bluish green in transmitted light.

boracite.name: Boracite
boracite.colors: Colorless, white, gray or yellow, bluish green to dark green if iron-bearing.

bowenite.name: Bowenite
bowenite.colors: Blue-green, yellow-green or dark green, and cream to blue-green in the cream-colored material.

brazilianite.name: Brazilianite
brazilianite.colors: Chartreuse-yellow, pale yellow and yellow-green, colorless in transmitted light.

brochantite.name: Brochantite
brochantite.colors: Emerald green, blackish green and pale green.

brown-diamond.name: Brown Diamond
brown-diamond.colors: Light brown with a yellow tint to deep brown with an orange tint.

brucite.name: Brucite
brucite.colors: Pale white, blue, gray or green, with manganoan brucite in yellow, reddish brown and dark brown.

bustamite.name: Bustamite
bustamite.colors: Light pastel pink to brownish red.

bytownite.name: Bytownite
bytownite.colors: Colorless, white or gray in the Handbook of Mineralogy, and pale yellow to brown in a faceting guide.

cacoxenite.name: Cacoxenite
cacoxenite.colors: Yellow to brownish yellow or reddish orange, also golden yellow, deep orange and rarely greenish.

canasite.name: Canasite
canasite.colors: Greenish yellow to grayish green per the mineral data, but the material sold as canasite is usually purplish.

cancrinite.name: Cancrinite
cancrinite.colors: Colorless, white, light blue to light grayish blue, honey-yellow, orange or reddish.

cavansite.name: Cavansite
cavansite.colors: Brilliant sky blue to greenish blue.

chabazite.name: Chabazite
chabazite.colors: Clear, white, pink, yellowish, reddish and brown.

chalcanthite.name: Chalcanthite
chalcanthite.colors: Berlin blue to sky blue and greenish blue, colorless to pale blue in transmitted light.

chalcopyrite.name: Chalcopyrite
chalcopyrite.colors: Brass yellow, tarnishing to gray green and sometimes iridescent.

chinese-writing-stone.name: Chinese Writing Stone
chinese-writing-stone.colors: Light colored feldspar crystals on a dark background.

chondrodite.name: Chondrodite
chondrodite.colors: Light yellow, yellow, brown and red.

chrome-chalcedony.name: Chrome Chalcedony
